name: Core AI vocabulary, French
summary: French terms of both tiers that the English core glossary (core.json) does not match: tier `ai` terms denote AI themselves, tier `context` terms are the lingo and the stand-ins around which French reports discuss AI without naming it. It applies only to filings whose language is fr, together with core.json, which matches the English terms these filings use unchanged (AI, machine learning, ChatGPT); phrases owned by core.json are not repeated. Built by going through the entries of core.json group by group, adding the French wording where French reports use one and the vocabulary of French and EU law and regulators (EU AI Act in French, RGPD, CNIL, ACPR, AMF, ANSSI, FranceTerme) where there is no English counterpart. Every term was found in a primary source, IATE, a French annual report or the French business press; phrases found nowhere were removed. Tiers follow core.json, lowered to `context` where the French wording is ambiguous (modèle, RIA, SIA, IAG). Phrases that end in IA are case-sensitive, so that the plural suffix does not match IAS (the accounting standards). Inflected forms (gender, plurals in -aux), unaccented spellings, both apostrophes and the ff/fi/fl ligatures that PDF conversion leaves are listed as variants (the ligature spellings as case-sensitive variants, in lower case and with a capital first letter, because the matcher folds a ligature into its letters when it removes duplicate phrases), because glossary.py only adds the English plural suffix. Status: hit-checked on the sample reports in gs://airo-eu-sample-reports and corrected against 33 annual reports from 17 ISIC sections (sector-sample/fr): wordings that the reports use and the glossary missed were added, variants that hit mostly outside AI were removed; to be checked by a native speaker.
